name: Sink-Sink
description: Sink-Sink is a card game commonly played in Niger; a variant of Agram with five cards per player instead of six, dealt in sets of three and two. Players follow suit; the winner of each trick leads to the next. The player who wins the fifth and last trick wins the game.

content.text: Sink-Sink is a card game commonly played in Niger; a variant of Agram with five cards per player instead of six, dealt in sets of three and two. Players follow suit; the winner of each trick leads to the next. The player who wins the fifth and last trick wins the game.

Country/Region of Origin: Niger
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: None

Type: 35 cards from standard 52-card pack (Kings, Queens, Jacks, Twos and Ace of Spades removed)
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Cards per Player: 5
Dealing Pattern: Three cards each, then two cards each (counter-clockwise from dealer)
First dealer: any player by agreement; thereafter winner of previous game deals next
